client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: During adult cardiac arrest, where should self-adhering defibrillation pads be placed?

options.A: On the exposed chest in either an anterolateral or anteroposterior position
options.B: Both pads on the same side of the chest
options.C: Directly over clothing so skin exposure is unnecessary
options.D: Anywhere on the torso because pad position does not affect current delivery

rationale: Current AHA adult basic life support guidance states that it is reasonable to place defibrillation pads on the exposed chest in an anterolateral or anteroposterior position. Direct skin contact is required for effective conduction, and pad placement is important to direct the energy vector toward the myocardium.
educational_objective: Identify acceptable current AHA pad positions for adult defibrillation.
source_document_title: 2025 CPR & ECC Guidelines, Part 7: Adult Basic Life Support
source_locator: Section 9.1 Pads for Defibrillation in Adult Cardiac Arrest
source_claim_supported: Supports anterolateral or anteroposterior placement on the exposed chest with direct skin contact.

correction_summary: Simplified the original placement wording to the exact AHA recommendation and removed unnecessary landmark precision not needed for the construct.
audit_findings: A directly matches the AHA recommendation; B-D are incompatible with correct energy delivery.
